title: Hobgoblins and George Hampton
summary: Parker left the Hobgoblins, a lodge band, to organize the Eureka; George Hampton is a barber now.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh, I played in the Hobgoblins.
And about how long had you played in the Hobgoblins before the Eureka?
Oh, I quit the Hobgoblins and made the Eureka. I organized the Eureka band.
But had the Hobgoblins been playing a long time?

The Hobgoblins played a good while. They had a band. And when I joined the Hobgoblins, it was a secret lodge, you know. And when I joined them, a fellow by his name, you ought to know him, George Hampton.
Well, he's a great musician. He's got a barbershop now right there on, right around the corner there.
Oh, he's about my age or younger.

Claiborne, yes, St. Cook. Uh-huh. Well, we'll find him on the—just as you turn, Claiborne on the riverside of the bank, on this side of the bank. How old does he look to you, my Kenry? I haven't seen him in the—
That's where Jim Crow gets his hair cut.
Yeah. He's a barbershop. He's a barbershop.
He's a barbershop. He's a barbershop. He's a barbershop.
